texts.preamble: Sriram vs Suhalya Travels Pvt Ltd on 14 August, 2025 Kabc020171072019 Before The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru. Dated This The 14th Day Of August 2025 Present: Sri.B.S.HONNASWAMY (B.A., Ll.M) Vii Addl. Scj and Acjm, Member, Mact-3, Bengaluru. M.V.C.No.3910/2019
texts.facts: The petitioners have filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against the respondents for seeking compensation on account of death of one Sri.Ajith @ Ajith Kumar S/o Sriram, in the Motor Vehicle Accident. 02. The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under: That on 04.12.2018 at about 11.50 p.m, the deceased Ajith @ Ajith Kumar was proceeding in the Omni Car bearing No.KA-03-MJ-2959 along with other friends and the same was driven by its driver from Bengaluru to Devanahalli, when they reached near (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.3910/2019 Kanmangala Palya Gate, BB Road, Devanahalli Taluk, at that time a Innova Car bearing No.KA-03-NB-9119 which belongs to respondent No.1, driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner, at very high speed, without giving any signal came from Bengaluru to Devanahalli and dashed to the Car from behind. Due to which the deceased sustained grievous injuries and immediately after the accident he was shifted to Government hospital, Devanahalli and after first aid, he was shifted to Shusrusha hospital and then shifted to Prolife hospital, Hebbala and admitted as inpatient for 120 days and finally on Sriram vs Suhalya Travels Pvt Ltd on 14 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113974092/ 3 02.04.2019 the doctor declared that he was dead. The petitioners have spent more than Rs.20,00,000/- towards medical expenses, food and nourishment charges, funeral and last rites. Prior to the accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 22 years and was doing private business as own work and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m and was the only bread winner in his family. Due to death of the deceased, the petitioners are put to great mental shock, irreparable loss and mental agony. The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending Innova Car and in this regard the BIAL Traffic Police have registered a case (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.3910/2019 against driver of the offending car in Crime No.173/2018 for the offences punishable U/Sec 279, 304(A) of IPC. The respondent No.1 is the RC Owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- to the petitioners together with interest at the rate of 18% p.a with costs. 03. On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels, but only the respondent No.2 has filed objections. Later the counsel for the petitioners have filed application to implead respondents No.3 to 8 as they are all Charge sheeted accused. Later notice was issued to respondents No.3 to 8. The respondents No.3 to 5 did not appeared and hence they were placed exparte. The respondents No.6 to 8 have are appeared before the tribunal, but not filed their objections. 04. The respondent No.2 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioners and further denied age, income, occupation of deceased and manner of accident, involvement of the vehicle, expenses incurred by the petitioners, dependency of the petitioners with the deceased and contended that the driver of the offending car was not holding valid (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.3910/2019 and effective driving licence at the time of accident as on the date of accident, the owner of the car has contravened the provisions of M.V. Act and Rules and they committed the breach of terms and conditions of the policy and admits that this respondent has issued policy of insurance in favour of respondent No.2 in respect of Car bearing No.KA-03-NB-9119 and the liability of this respondent if any, is limited to terms and conditions of the policy. The car in question did not involved in the accident nor caused accidental injuries to the petitioner and on the date of accident the car was being driven in a reasonable speed and careful manner and there was no rashness or negligence on the part of the driver of car and the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the omni car, in which deceased persons and petitioner were travelling. The petition is bad for non-joinder of proper and necessary parties. The compensation claimed is highly excessive, exaggerated and hence, pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.2. 05. Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed by my learned predecessor: - (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.3910/2019 ISSUES Sriram vs Suhalya Travels Pvt Ltd on 14 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113974092/ 4 06. In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 was got examined as PW.1 and got marked 22 documents as Ex.P.1 to 22 and closed their side evidence. 07. By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.2 did not lead evidence inspite of sufficient opportunity has been given.
texts.arguments: As (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.3910/2019 per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 15 to 25 years is "18". In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.3910/2019 Pranay Sethi & Others case, the future prospects or additional income should be added to monthly income of the deceased. Since deceased was aged below 40 years and was self employee at the time of accident, 40% income should be added to the monthly income towards future prospects which would be result in the income to be (12,500 + 5,000) = Rs.17,500/-. The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.8,750/-. 17. In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case in respect to loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.3910/2019 10% in every 3 years. Accordingly, in the head of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses, 10% is enhanced for period of every 3 years. In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported Sriram vs Suhalya Travels Pvt Ltd on 14 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113974092/ 7 in Magma (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.3910/2019 General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram alias Churu Ram reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, the petitioner No.3 is entitled for Rs.40,000/- towards loss of love and affection and petitioners are entitled for Rs.19,500/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses and transportation of dead body. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and noticing the number of dependents and 50% of the income taken into consideration towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased, this Tribunal has placed reliance on ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & others case has calculated compensation as under; Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount in Rs. 1. Loss of Dependency (After 18,90,000-00 deducting 50% of the income towards personal and living expenses) 2. Loss of filial consortium 96,800-00 (For petitioners No.1 and 2) 3. Loss of love and affection 40,000-00 (For petitioner No.3) 4. Loss of estate 19,500-00 (SCCH-3) 17 M.V.C.No.3910/2019 5. 6. Medical expenses 17,86,318-00 Total 38,52,118-00 20.
